text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing nvme read latency spikes on ephemeral pools in us-west2, GPU provisioning is stalling on a few jobs. hitting EIO on /dev/nvme0n1 during checkpoint restore :frowning:
infra-bot: ALERT: nvme-read-latency spike on pool gn-usw2-ephemeral (10 hosts) — avg read latency 15ms -> 120ms over 12m window.
aj: which hosts? can you paste a short iostat/smart snippet and the failing restore log lines?
maria: gnode-uw2-07, gnode-uw2-09, gnode-uw2-11. quick tail from restore: 
```
2026-03-18T02:10:15Z restore: open(/mnt/ephemeral/checkpoint-xyz): read error: errno=5
2026-03-18T02:10:16Z restore: retrying chunk 42/128
2026-03-18T02:10:17Z restore: read timeout after 3s
```
And iostat snippet: 
```
Device            tps    rMB/s   wMB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await
nvme0n1         420.1   85.2     1.3      221.3    10.2     25.4
```
sung: that's suspicious — we pushed the scrub scheduler change yesterday to compress metadata writes. could be causing background GC/wear leveling to spike IO. any firmware updates rolled recently?
tess: kernel backport landed on a subset (nvme fixes) last week for uw2 hosts, but we didn't target those gnodes specifically. i'll check the deployment list.
kevin: temporary mitigation: reduce concurrent checkpoint restores per node (we've been doing 8 concurrently). suggest throttling to 2-3 until scrub window finishes. also consider fallback to remote fetch from s3 for cold restores. tradeoff: higher egress and slower finishes but preserves provisioning throughput.
aj: agree. can we wire a short-term scheduler change? Even a 4-min window where provisioning controllers prefer nodes with <30% nvme-util.
ops-oncall: i'm throttling provisioning for the affected AZs now (reduced batch size by 50%), which freed some queue. noticed a 30% drop in failed allocations already.
maria: thanks. adding a small diagnostic: `sudo nvme get-feature -f 0x0c -H /dev/nvme0n1` and `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` gave some reallocation counts up but not catastrophic. paste below: 
```
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 12
Media_Wearout_Indicator: 6
```
so wear is nonzero but not extreme. pattern looks like read amplification during restores.
sung: ok that aligns with scrub/GC speculative IO. action items: roll back scrub aggressive window for us-west2, lower restore concurrency to 3, and enable remote-fetch fallback for long restores ( > 90s ).
tess: rollback scheduled in 5m to config set `ephemeral.scrub.window=offpeak` for us-west2 — will post when done.
kevin: also propose an longer-term: prefer checkpoint layout that streams directly from objectstore when snapshot size > 8GB or when local nvme avgqu-sz > 5. avoids overloading small drives. need cost estimate for egress.
aj: cost note — current egress for a 12GB restore across 100 restores/day -> ~1.2TB egress -> ~$90/mo equivalent. pretty cheap compared to lost GPU minutes.
ops-oncall: scrub rollback done. metrics look better at t+7m. still 2 hosts with intermittent EIO, opening hardware tickets to vendor.
maria: thanks — i'll run through a small canary to cap concurrent restores. sharing a quick one-liner to deploy via runbook: 
```
for h in gnode-uw2-07 gnode-uw2-09 gnode-uw2-11; do 
  ssh $h "sudo echo 3 > /proc/sys/infra/restore_concurrency"
done
```
kevin: can we make that a controller-level soft limit instead so we don't need host ssh? upstream PR queued: infra/controller#452.
sung: please add a regression check — restore throughput vs nvme-util — in the rollout. we don't want silent perf regressions.
aj: i'll add an alert: provisioning-latency when > 60s and nvme avgqu-sz > 8 for >2m.
ops-oncall: created incident ticket INF-2026-418, tagging hw + infra.
maria: summary: immediate: cap per-node restore concurrency, rollback scrub schedule, throttle provisioning in us-west2. mid-term: remote-fetch fallback heuristics + controller soft limit + vendor hw ticket. i'll follow up with Ops doc and a postmortem if the hardware tickets confirm failures. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks — can we revisit default concurrency in the optimize recommendations? sounds like we tuned too aggressively for raw throughput and forgot local nvme variability.
maria: agreed. will add to next week's infra retro.
